extra.message: Jelleo SOL-016: a stored `.bump` is read. Risk: a non-canonical bump — reused via an Anchor `bump = <account>.bump` constraint, or read and fed to `create_program_address` (both accept non-canonical bumps → PDA substitution). SAFE only if the SAME account's bump was set at init via Anchor's bare `bump`/`ctx.bumps` (canonical), NOT a caller-supplied `#[instruction(bump)]` value — verify that init, then dismiss; otherwise it's the bug. For non-constraint reads compare to `find_program_address(seeds, &program_id).1`. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-016.

sss-exclusions: the read is `bump = <account>.bump` (or a bare `seeds = [...], bump` with NO `= target` after bump) on a typed `Account<'info, T>`, AND the SAME account's stored bump was written at init by Anchor's bare `bump` / `ctx.bumps.<name>` (canonical) — NOT a caller-supplied `#[instruction(bump)]` value and NOT a value from create_program_address: verify that exact init site, then dismiss (idiomatic canonical reuse, not a finding). If the init bump is caller-supplied or otherwise non-canonical, this reuse IS the bug — keep it (Anchor's `bump = <expr>` re-derives via create_program_address with the GIVEN bump, so a non-canonical stored bump still validates).
a non-constraint read is validated against the canonical bump before use (e.g. require!(stored == Pubkey::find_program_address(seeds, program_id).1))

the PDA (and its bump) is created in the same instruction using the canonical bump from find_program_address (NOT a caller-supplied bump passed to create_program_address, which accepts any valid off-curve bump and re-introduces the non-canonical-bump bug)
